Gokarṇa
(‘the ear of the cow’)
------------------------------------------
Out of the three extremely important places of पिल्ग्रिमगे for the devotees of Lord शिव, गोकर्ण is also one. The other two are काशी (Vārāṇasi) and रामेश्वरम्. The three together are called ‘Tristhalī’.
Gokarṇa is on the west coast in South India. It is situated in the Kumta taluk of the North Canara (or Uttarakannada) district of the Karnataka State.
The story goes that रावण, the demon king of लङ्का, secured the ātmaliṅga (the शिवलिङ्ग containing the very essence and power of Lord शिव) from शिव himself and was bringing it in his hands with a view to establishing it in his capital city. Since this would have ended in catastrophe for the gods as well as the human beings, the gods worked out a stratagem by which गणपति disguised as a young ब्रह्मचारिन् would see that the लिङ्ग is some how placed on the ground. At the approach of sunset, रावण wanted to perform his evening सन्ध्या ritual. He gave charge of the लिङ्ग to the boy गणपति who was found loitering nearby, with the special instruction that it should not be placed on the ground since it would then get stuck permanently. गणपति accepted the responsibility stipulating the condition that रावण should come back before he is called thrice, to return. गणपति however, managed to call रावण three times before he could finish his सन्ध्या, and kept the लिङ्ग on the ground. It got permanently fixed there.
After punishing गणपति by a severe punch on his head, रावण tried all his might to uproot the लिङ्ग but to no avail. In the process, the लिङ्ग got deformed into the shape of a गोकर्ण or the ear of a cow. Hence the name ‘Gokarṇa’ for the place of पिल्ग्रिमगे that sprang up there.
The शिवलिङ्ग is known as ‘Mahā-baleśvara’ (‘Īśvara of infinite might’) since even the mighty रावण could not move it even by an inch!
The whole लिङ्ग is under the ground and hardly 5 cms. (2 inches) of it is seen above.
The temple is considered as very old and belongs probably to the early christian era.
The sanctum is about 5.1 metres (17 ft.) square. The कलश or pinial is made of brass. The height of the विमान (tower over the sanctum) is 18 metres (60 ft.). The raṅgamaṇṭapa (hall in front of the sanctum) is 18 metres by 9 metres (60 ft. by 30 ft.).
Images of पार्वती, गणपति and नन्दि have been established round the main shrine.
The icon of गणपति here is in the standing posture and is a little peculiar in appearance. It is considered as very ancient (A.

to 700).
Mahāśivarātri is the biggest of the festivals observed here. The रथोत्सव (temple car festival) is held on Phālguna śukla pratipad (first day of the bright fortnight in the month Phālguna, usually in February/March).
Koṭitīrtha is the biggest of the temple tanks where the pilgrims bathe before visiting the temple. Some of the other bathing places are: Bindutīrtha, अगस्त्य-tīrtha, Jaṭāyutīrtha, रामतीर्थ, Pāṇḍava-tīrtha and so on. For those who undertake the पिल्ग्रिमगे to गोकर्ण as a religious ritual, the following are prescribed: bath in the Koṭitīrtha, ड़स्तिन्ग्, śrāddha to the forefathers, bath in the sea, pūjās at the main temple and other temples and giving of gifts.
Two more Gokarṇas have been mentioned in the पुराणस् as existing near the सरस्वती रिवेर् and मथुरा (in Uttar Pradesh). But they are not well-known now.
Gokarṇa is the name of the saintly person mentioned in the Padmapurāṇa (vide Uttarakhaṇḍa chs. 4 and 5). Born of a barren cow due to the grace of a monk, गोकर्ण had a human body with a cow’s ears. Hence the name ‘Gokarṇa.’ His devoted recital of the famous purāṇa, the Bhāgavata, brought लिबेरतिओन् to all the hearers.

Gokula
(‘the abode of cows’)
------------------------------------------
Gokula or Nandagokula was the village where the child कृष्ण (and his elder brother बलराम) spent his childhood days. It was a fertile and prosperous village of the cowherds situated on the bank of the river यमुना. नन्द was the chieftain of the village. However, after कृष्ण was attacked by a number of demons sent by Kaṁsa—who were all, of course, destroyed by him—the people of the village migrated to the nearby Vṛndāvana, also on the bank of the यमुना river.
The modern गोकुल is about 8 kms. from मथुरा (in Uttar Pradesh), lower down the stream, but on the opposite bank of the यमुना river. It is now the Head-quarters of the वल्लभ sect of the Vaiṣṇavas.
